messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: prod /v1/stream p99 latency breach in us-east-1. Current p95=1.1s p99=2.6s (SLO p99 1.2s). Alert triggered 09:17 UTC. Auto-tag: continuous-batching-path.

oncall-alex: ack — I'm on it. started pulling traces.

oncall-alex: quick snapshot from traces: most p99 traces show long queue wait on batch scheduler, then streaming stalls after first token. Looks like big batches + mixed sequence lengths.

sre-jamie: seeing same in dashboards. tail latency spike across replica pool rpool-3. Throughput steady, errors ~0. No recent deploys.

infra-sam: rolling capacity is healthy. No infra-related network errors.

oncall-alex: mitigation idea — disable continuous batching path for streaming endpoints to force single-request handling for hot paths. Will flip feature flag and reduce max_batch_size.

oncall-alex: issuing change now:
```
# disable continuous batching for streaming route
redwoodctl apply-config --env=prod 
  --path=runtime.streaming.continuous_batching.enabled=false
# reduce max batch size to limit head-of-line waits
redwoodctl apply-config --env=prod 
  --path=runtime.batch.max_size=32
```

rtm-bot: Config apply queued; will rollout to rpool-3 in 60s.

sre-jamie: watch metrics: p99 should start dropping if queue waits are culprit. Also switching scheduler fairness to 'stratified' might help — current is 'size-aware' which groups by length but seems to let extremely long seqs dominate.

eng-runtime-lee: we have a known issue: continuous batching builds batches by arrival time and does not preempt long sequences. Mixed sequences (short chat + long doc summary) create stally batches. We shipped fix in staging last month but didn't promote to prod.

customer-success-lina: FYI we've had 3 customers open realtime support threads in last 20m complaining about slow streaming for interactive features. Escalated to enterprise SREs.

oncall-alex: p99 dropped to 1.4s 2m after flag flip. p95 stable. Still above SLO but improved. Continuing.

infra-sam: rolling restart of rpool-3 workers (one node at a time) to pick up config; starting now.

sre-jamie: after restart p99 = 1.18s, p95=0.9s. Looks within SLO boundaries for now. Need to keep watch for 15m.

oncall-alex: customer impact: intermittent slow streams for ~09:12–09:22 UTC for us-east-1; approx 0.6% of requests hit p99>2s window. CS notified. Lina, can you log customers + incident window?

customer-success-lina: copying notes into support tracker now, pinged account leads for affected customers. No escalations to legal/compliance so far.

eng-runtime-lee: action items from quick triage:
- promote batching-preemptive fix from staging to prod on canary.
- implement temporary scheduler change: stratify by (seq_len_bucket, arrival) to reduce long seq head-of-line.
- longer-term: adaptive batching by sequence-length prediction and KV-cache-aware splitting.

sre-jamie: file an incident ticket with preliminary severity: Sev2 (SLO breach, limited customer impact). Add timeline and mitigations.

oncall-alex: handing off to night oncall in 45m. @sre-jamie please keep watch, @eng-runtime-lee can you queue the canary deploy for the preemptive-batching patch?

eng-runtime-lee: will open PR and request urgent canary; ETA ~30m for canary build then smoke tests. If green, we'll promote.

rtm-bot: Canary build started for commit b3f9ad. smoke tests in progress.

sre-jamie: monitoring note: set synthetic probes for /v1/stream with mixed short+long payloads every 1m across us-east-1 to catch regressions.

oncall-alex: handoff summary for night:
- state: p99 breach resolved after disabling continuous batching + reducing batch size + rolling restart.
- impact: small fraction of requests high tail during window; CS notified.
- next steps: canary preemptive-batching fix, scheduler policy tweak, postmortem.
- oncall to monitor p99, worker queue lengths, and synthetic probes.

sre-jamie: noted. I'll keep an eye and notify if p99 > 1.3s sustained for 5m.

customer-success-lina: will update customers with timeline + next steps once we have canary outcome.

eng-runtime-lee: after canary (if green) we'll schedule rollout and include feature-flag gating so we can quickly revert. Also adding telemetry to measure batch composition (seq length distribution per batch) for postmortem.

oncall-alex: thanks all. handoff complete. @incident-bot mark incident: in-mitigation -> monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-14-1778504321 state changed: IN_MITIGATION -> MONITORING. Assigned: eng-runtime-lee, oncall: sre-jamie.

sre-jamie: quick root-cause hypothesis for postmortem: continuous batching + size-aware scheduler allowed long-sequence requests to block batches, causing queue wait amplification and streaming stalls for short/interactive requests.

eng-runtime-lee: agreed. Planned postmortem will include: timeline, graphs (p95/p99 pre/post), batch composition heatmaps, config changes, and action owner list (deploy, scheduler change, telemetry).

oncall-alex: adding retrospective note: consider lower default max_batch_size for streaming endpoints and expose per-route batching profile.

customer-success-lina: noted — I'll coordinate follow-up comms once we have the full postmortem.

sre-jamie: I'll close out thread when postmortem draft is uploaded.

oncall-alex: thanks, logging out. good job team. :thumbsup:
